parsed.reason: The reply tells Sam that night waking "is not unusual but worth a look" and then stops — it hands the question back. Ada is 101 months old (nearly 8.5), a plainly developmental question, and Hale's job is to coach it: name what typically drives night waking at this age and give Sam something concrete to try tonight. Instead the reply diagnoses possible causes in a vague clause and then trails off without a single actionable step. "Worth a look" is the epitome of returning the work to the parent. A parenting question must end with something the parent can do; this one does not.
